info.title: ZROtext sealed API v1 message plane (proposed contract)
info.description: PROPOSAL ONLY, derived from the ZT-009 decisions recorded 2026-09-26 in protocol/drafts/zt-009-decision-log.md (rows Q4, Q6, Q8, Q9 and Q11). NO server route implementing this contract exists yet and the sealed runtime remains disabled: no production client may emit or accept a sealed profile-01/02 envelope, and no relay handler is mounted at either path. This document is the proposed HTTP surface for task 21 slice 1 so later slices can implement, review and audit against a pinned contract. The synthetic alpha plane (/v1/alpha/messages, an allowlisted fixed-body test route) and the closed general send plane stay separate: sealed credentials must not be accepted on alpha routes, alpha credentials must not be accepted on sealed routes, and no sealed envelope is ever translated into a synthetic-alpha submission (Q11). Sealed device, webhook and usage endpoints are DEFERRED to later slices of task 21 and intentionally absent here. Both operations accept ONLY the exact raw-binary content type application/vnd.zrotext.sealed.v1: there is no JSON request body, no plaintext body field, no downgrade flag and no plaintext fallback retry anywhere in this contract.

post.summary: Submit one sealed outbound envelope for device dispatch
post.description: Proposed contract; no route exists. The request body is exactly one complete sealed outbound envelope (profile kind 01) as raw binary bytes with the exact content type application/vnd.zrotext.sealed.v1. The relay never decrypts: it verifies the owner-pinned manifest chain, the allowed device signing key and scope, and the device signature over the exact unsigned bytes, then compares the protected account/device/line/manifest fields with the authenticated identity and database state. Idempotency is the SHA-256 digest of the unsigned envelope bytes (Q6): an identical replay returns the stored message identity with created=false and performs no new dispatch; no caller-supplied idempotency-key header is accepted. Admission fails closed when the active manifest is expired or was issued too far in the future (Q4), and clock-rollback or restored-high-water conditions require fresh owner-verified enrollment (Q4). The plaintext inside the ciphertext is a strict UTF-8 body of 1-32,768 bytes with no BOM, no NUL, no Unicode normalization and no padding in v1 (Q9); body length, recipient, timing and segment-count leakage is disclosed and accepted. Every response carries Cache-Control: no-store.

requestBody.description: One complete sealed outbound envelope (kind 01) as raw bytes. Bounds: the envelope is at least 426 bytes, at most 34,213 bytes for kind 01, and the request-body limit is the 36,864-byte pre-allocation cap. A JSON body, any other content type, an unknown profile or kind, a set downgrade flag, or trailing bytes is rejected (Q11).

202.description: Accepted for dispatch, or an identical replay no-op. Acceptance means durable storage of the exact envelope bytes and queueing toward the bound device; it never means carrier submission. Idempotency is on the unsigned envelope digest (Q6): replaying byte-identical unsigned content returns the existing message identity with created=false.

400.description: invalid_request: the bytes are not a bounded, exactly parsed sealed envelope, or verification of the manifest chain, signing key/scope or device signature failed, or a client-allocated identity is malformed. future_manifest: the manifest's issued_at is more than five minutes ahead of trusted server time (Q4); resubmitting unchanged will not help until the manifest is reissued.

401.description: unauthorized: missing, malformed or unknown bearer credential.

403.description: forbidden: the credential is not authorized for the tenant, line or device named in the envelope, or the key is revoked or wrong-role. stale_manifest: the active manifest has expired (its exclusive expiry passed, or its lifetime exceeds 24 hours), which blocks sealed outbound fail-closed until a fresh manifest is pinned (Q4). re_enrollment_required: a device-clock rollback or a restored high-water store was detected; sealed submission stays refused until fresh owner-verified enrollment (Q4).

409.description: idempotency_conflict: a client-allocated identity in the protected record was already stored under a different unsigned envelope digest (Q6); the earlier envelope stays authoritative and this submission creates nothing.

415.description: unsupported_media_type: the request did not use exactly application/vnd.zrotext.sealed.v1. A JSON body, a multipart body, or any other content type is rejected here and is never parsed as a sealed envelope, translated to the synthetic-alpha route, or retried as plaintext (Q11).

429.description: rate_limited, queue_full or quota_exceeded: the account or device exceeded its sealed admission budget.

503.description: unavailable or billing_pending: storage or dispatch is temporarily unavailable; retry later with the same envelope bytes.

post.summary: Upload one sealed inbound event captured by a device
post.description: Proposed contract; no route exists. This is the separate sealed inbound route required by Q8: it writes the separate sealed_inbound_events store and must never be routed through the M1 outbound-attempt inbound pilot. The request body is exactly one complete sealed inbound envelope (profile kind 02) as raw binary bytes with the exact content type application/vnd.zrotext.sealed.v1. The phone allocates one stable 16-byte event_id for the normalized logical SMS, journals text, event ID and a positive device-local sequence before sealing, and retries replay the exact envelope bytes. The server compares the (account, device, event_id) identity and the (device, device_sequence) replay fence against the unsigned envelope digest: an identical replay is a no-op success with created=false; a changed event under the same identity or a reused device sequence fails with 409. Out-of-order arrival is accepted within a seven-day observed-time window (Q8). Tombstone retention is an operational constraint: event-ID and device-sequence tombstones must be retained at least eight days after first acceptance, because deleting a row without a durable fence would permit replay. When the active manifest is expired the device quarantines the event locally until a fresh manifest rather than uploading (Q4); if an expired-manifest upload still arrives, the server fails closed. Clock-rollback or restored-high-water conditions require fresh owner-verified enrollment (Q4). The plaintext inside the ciphertext is a strict UTF-8 body of 1-32,768 bytes with no BOM, no NUL, no Unicode normalization and no padding in v1 (Q9). Every response carries Cache-Control: no-store and never echoes envelope content.

requestBody.description: One complete sealed inbound envelope (kind 02) as raw bytes. Bounds: the envelope is at least 426 bytes, at most 34,082 bytes for kind 02, and the request-body limit is the 36,864-byte pre-allocation cap. A JSON body, any other content type, an unknown profile or kind, or a set downgrade flag is rejected (Q11).

202.description: Stored, or an identical replay no-op. created=false means this exact (account, device, event_id) with the same unsigned digest was already accepted and nothing new was created. Out-of-order arrival is accepted within the seven-day observed-time window (Q8). Acceptance is durable storage only; webhook fanout is a deferred separate contract.

400.description: invalid_request: the bytes are not a bounded, exactly parsed sealed envelope, or verification of the manifest chain, signing key/scope or device signature failed. future_manifest: the manifest's issued_at is more than five minutes ahead of trusted server time (Q4). stale_event: the observed time falls outside the seven-day observed-time window (Q8).

401.description: unauthorized: missing, malformed or unknown bearer credential.

403.description: forbidden: the credential is not authorized for the tenant, line or device named in the protected record, the line binding is not active at the current generation, or the key is revoked or wrong-role. stale_manifest: the manifest has expired; the device should have quarantined the event locally until a fresh manifest (Q4), and the server fails closed. re_enrollment_required: a device-clock rollback or a restored high-water store was detected; upload stays refused until fresh owner-verified enrollment (Q4).

409.description: event_id_conflict: this event_id was already accepted for the account and device with a different unsigned digest (changed content). sequence_conflict: this (device, device_sequence) was already consumed by a different event. Both are conflicting replays under the Q8 fences; the stored event stays authoritative and the conflicting upload creates nothing.

415.description: unsupported_media_type: the request did not use exactly application/vnd.zrotext.sealed.v1. A JSON body, a multipart body, or any other content type is rejected here and is never parsed as a sealed envelope, translated to the synthetic-alpha route, or retried as plaintext (Q11).

429.description: rate_limited, queue_full or quota_exceeded: the account or device exceeded its sealed admission budget.

503.description: unavailable or billing_pending: storage is temporarily unavailable; retry later with the exact same envelope bytes, event ID and sequence.

bearerAuth.description: The existing customer API-key authentication, not a new auth model: an account API key issued by the owner API-key routes under /v1/auth and sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>', exactly as the existing message routes authenticate. Outbound submission requires the existing message-send scope bound to the device named in the envelope's protected record; inbound upload requires a credential authorized for the uploading device, and the protected account, device and line fields must match the authenticated identity and the active line-binding generation. This HTTP layer only names the tenant: the sealed manifest chain and device signature over the exact unsigned bytes carry the cryptographic authorization (Q2, Q7). Sealed and alpha credentials stay separate (Q11).

NoStore.description: Every sealed response is non-cacheable, mirroring the existing message routes.

SealedEnvelopeBytes.description: One complete sealed envelope as raw binary bytes: the exact profile bytes including the fixed prefix, protected record, body ciphertext, recipient wraps and signature. Never JSON, never base64-wrapped, never a multipart part. The encrypted plaintext is a strict UTF-8 body of 1-32,768 bytes with no BOM, no NUL, no Unicode normalization and no padding in v1 (Q9).

SealedOutboundAccepted.description: Acceptance metadata for a sealed outbound envelope. Contains no recipient, no plaintext and no envelope bytes.

message_id.description: The server-allocated message identity for the accepted envelope; identical on digest replays.

created.description: false when this exact unsigned envelope digest was already accepted (idempotent replay, Q6).

SealedInboundAccepted.description: Acceptance metadata for a sealed inbound event. Contains no sender, no plaintext and no envelope bytes.

event_id.description: The phone-allocated stable event identity echoed back from the protected record.

created.description: false when this exact (account, device, event_id) with the same unsigned digest was already accepted (no-op replay, Q8).

Error.description: The existing error shape used by the message routes: a single machine-readable code and no content echo.

code.description: Lowercase snake_case machine code for the admission failure; the response description defines the taxonomy.
